title: Listener and inner-class leaks
key_conclusions: Listener leaks are retained-path problems through registry, manager, adapter, observable, listener, callback, lambda, this$0, or captured fields rather than a generic inner-class problem.
Anonymous inner classes and Kotlin lambdas become dangerous when a longer-lived owner stores them after they have captured Activity, Fragment, View, binding, or Context objects.
The unregister boundary must match the owner and victim lifecycle: Activity onDestroy/onStop, Fragment onDestroyView, ViewHolder recycling, removeObserver, dispose, or Job cancellation.
A listener leak fix should be accepted only with before/after evidence from LeakCanary, HPROF Path To GC Roots, listener list counts, dumpsys meminfo trends, or source-path verification.
shallow_points: The article still uses representative retained paths rather than a real target-app HPROF.
It does not decode a real LeakCanary listener, observeForever, or adapter callback trace line by line with concrete app class names.
It does not validate AndroidX LiveData, Fragment, RecyclerView, RxJava, or coroutine method names against specific dependency versions.
It does not include live instrumentation that prints registry/listener counts before and after lifecycle callbacks.
